scenario.title: First Time in Japan, No Regrets
scenario.summary: A Japan-first-timer scenario designed to stop players from building a chaotic checklist trip and instead guide them toward a route with actual taste, pacing, and payoff.

guide.name: Ren
guide.systemStyle: Give practical travel advice with a point of view. Prefer strong recommendations over mushy option-dumping. Call out bad itinerary instincts directly but not cruelly.

tokyo.title: Tokyo
tokyo.tradeoff: Easy to overstuff if you confuse movement with having a good time.

kyoto.title: Kyoto
kyoto.tradeoff: Can feel over-touristed and logistically annoying if you stay in the wrong area.

osaka.title: Osaka
osaka.tradeoff: Often added because it feels efficient, not because the player actually wants a third base.

hakone.title: Hakone
hakone.tradeoff: A great punctuation mark, a bad checklist add-on.

nara.title: Nara
nara.tradeoff: Good if you already have Kyoto; less compelling if it turns the whole trip into one more transfer.

kamakura.title: Kamakura
kamakura.tradeoff: Only smart if the player wants breathing room, not accumulation.

uji.title: Uji
uji.tradeoff: Subtler payoff than Nara; better for taste than bragging rights.

kanazawa.title: Kanazawa
kanazawa.tradeoff: Too ambitious for this exact scenario unless the player sacrifices elsewhere.

turns.guideMessage: You have 8 days and enough budget to do this properly, but not enough time to be stupid about it. What do you actually want this trip to feel like?

choices.label: Food-heavy and atmospheric
choices.playerReply: I want food, neighborhoods, and atmosphere more than a giant checklist.

choices.label: Electric and urban
choices.playerReply: Give me neon, late nights, and city energy.

choices.label: Balanced: city + calm
choices.playerReply: I want city life without frying my nervous system.

choices.label: Temples, design, and slower mornings
choices.playerReply: I care more about atmosphere and beauty than constant stimulation.

turns.guideMessage: Good. Now let's decide whether you're taking a trip or collecting train platforms. How many bases are we doing?

choices.label: Tokyo + Kyoto
choices.playerReply: Two bases. Tokyo and Kyoto. Clean and sane.

choices.label: Tokyo + Kyoto + Osaka
choices.playerReply: Three cities. I want range.

choices.label: Tokyo only, deeply done
choices.playerReply: One city done properly beats a shallow grand tour.

choices.label: Tokyo + Kyoto with one scenic reset
choices.playerReply: Tokyo, Kyoto, and one deliberate contrast point.

turns.guideMessage: Where you sleep matters more than people admit. A smart location can save a trip. A dumb one can turn it into a commuter sim.

choices.label: Prioritize a smart central location
choices.playerReply: I'd rather spend a bit more than waste my trip in transit.

choices.label: Save money with a cheaper out-of-the-way stay
choices.playerReply: I'll save on the room and deal with the location tradeoff.

choices.label: Splurge only in one city
choices.playerReply: Let's be smart about where comfort matters most.

turns.guideMessage: One or two precise splurges create better memories than vague luxury everywhere. Where do you want the money to actually matter?

choices.label: A ryokan night
choices.playerReply: Give me one proper ryokan night.

choices.label: One unforgettable meal
choices.playerReply: I want one meal that becomes part of the story.

choices.label: Better hotel locations
choices.playerReply: Honestly, spend where it improves the whole trip.

turns.guideMessage: Travel internet wants you to add a day trip. Sometimes that's smart. Sometimes it's itinerary tax. What's the move?

choices.label: Add Nara
choices.playerReply: Nara feels like the cleanest add-on.

choices.label: Add Hakone
choices.playerReply: Let's use one day for scenery and reset energy.

choices.label: Skip the day trip and stay local
choices.playerReply: No bonus detour. Let the trip breathe.

choices.label: Do a quieter Uji side trip
choices.playerReply: If we add something, I want it to feel subtle rather than obvious.

turns.guideMessage: Forecast update: your Kyoto stretch is getting a wet day. You can either fight reality or adapt like an adult. What's the adjustment?

choices.label: Lean into indoor culture and long meals
choices.playerReply: Fine. Let's make the rain part of the atmosphere.

choices.label: Keep the outdoor plan anyway
choices.playerReply: We'll push through. Weather doesn't get to win.

choices.label: Re-sequence the route to protect the best day
choices.playerReply: Let's move things around and save the best outdoor stretch for better weather.

turns.guideMessage: Let's decide what 'good food' actually means to you, because that phrase gets abused. What are we optimizing for?

choices.label: Local spots and neighborhood meals
choices.playerReply: I care more about texture and atmosphere than prestige.

choices.label: A smart mix of casual and one great splurge
choices.playerReply: I want range, not just one version of eating well.

choices.label: Big-name places and signature meals
choices.playerReply: If there's one trip to chase the classics, this is it.

turns.guideMessage: Last important Kyoto decision: where are you staying? This is the difference between elegant and annoying.

choices.label: Stay somewhere atmospheric and walkable
choices.playerReply: I want mornings and evenings that actually feel like Kyoto.

choices.label: Stay near Kyoto Station for convenience
choices.playerReply: Let's optimize for movement and simplicity.

choices.label: Stay farther out to save money
choices.playerReply: Budget first. We'll cope with the friction.

turns.guideMessage: You're near the end. One last choice: do we spend the final stretch chasing one more thing, or do we let the trip land cleanly?

choices.label: Leave one final evening mostly unplanned
choices.playerReply: I'd rather have space than one more forced memory.

choices.label: Pack in one more famous thing
choices.playerReply: It's my first trip. I want one last iconic swing.

choices.label: End with one meal or bar worth remembering
choices.playerReply: No extra landmark. Give me one final scene.

turns.guideMessage: Good. We have enough to call this a trip instead of a spreadsheet with delusions.

endingVariants.travelerType: A high-taste traveler who likes cities best when they still leave room to breathe.
endingVariants.summary: You built a coherent first Japan trip with enough atmosphere, enough appetite, and not too much transit stupidity.
endingVariants.biggestWin: You avoided turning a dream trip into a luggage relay race.

endingVariants.biggestWin: You learned exactly where your tolerance for movement ends.

endingVariants.travelerType: A depth-first traveler who would rather know one place properly than skim three badly.
endingVariants.summary: You resisted scope creep and built a trip with unusually good texture for a first-timer.
endingVariants.biggestWin: You left room for surprise instead of replacing it with logistics.

defaultEnding.summary: You built a solid first Japan trip with enough shape to be real and enough flexibility to still feel alive.
defaultEnding.biggestWin: You made tradeoffs on purpose instead of by accident.
